facts.statement: Ophthalmosaurus lived from the Middle Jurassic to the Late Jurassic, with possible remains from the earliest Cretaceous (Berriasian). (Callovian to Oxfordian)
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Jurassic to Late Jurassic (Callovian to Oxfordian), Possible record during the Berriasian

facts.statement: The genus Ophthalmosaurus was first described by Harry Seeley in 1874. (Seeley, 1874)
facts.quote: authority: Seeley, 1874

facts.statement: Ophthalmosaurus was a medium-sized ichthyosaur reaching 4 meters in length and weighing 940 kilograms. (4 m long and weighing 940 kg)
facts.quote: It was a relatively medium-sized ichthyosaur, measuring 4 m long and weighing 940 kg.

facts.statement: Harry Seeley described Ophthalmosaurus in 1874, focusing on clavicular bone morphology. (Harry Seeley in 1874)
facts.quote: Ophthalmosaurus was first described by Harry Seeley in 1874 with particular focus on the morphology of the clavicular bones.

facts.statement: Ophthalmosaurus lived from the Middle Jurassic to the early Late Jurassic, between 165 and 157 million years ago. (entre 165 a 157 millones de años)
facts.quote: que vivió durante el Jurásico Medio hasta principios del Jurásico Superior (entre 165 a 157 millones de años)

facts.statement: Ophthalmosaurus gave birth by pushing its young out tail-first to prevent them from drowning.
facts.quote: Como otros ictiosaurios, Ophthalmosaurus paría a sus crías sacándolas primero por la cola, evitándoles ahogarse.

facts.statement: Fossil skeletons of unborn young found in nearly fifty females show that litters ranged from two to eleven offspring.
facts.quote: Esqueletos de jóvenes no nacidos han sido hallados en cerca de cincuenta hembras en hallazgos fósiles, y el tamaño de las camadas iba de dos a once crías.

facts.statement: Ophthalmosaurus had a teardrop-shaped body and a crescent-shaped tail fin.
facts.quote: Ophthalmosaurus tenía un cuerpo con forma de lágrima y una aleta caudal similar a una medialuna

facts.statement: Its front flippers were more developed than its hind limbs, suggesting the front flippers steered while the tail provided propulsion.
facts.quote: Sus miembros delanteros estaban más desarrollados que los traseros, lo que sugiere que las aletas frontales timoneaban mientras la cola realizaba la propulsión.

facts.statement: Ophthalmosaurus is famous for its large eyes, which reached a diameter of 10.16 centimeters.
facts.quote: La fama de Ophthalmosaurus se debe sobre todo a sus grandes ojos que alcanzaban 10.16 centímetros de diámetro

facts.statement: The eyes occupied almost the entire skull space and were protected by bony plates called the scleral ring, likely to maintain eye shape against deep-water pressure.
facts.quote: Los ojos ocupaban casi todo el espacio en el cráneo y estaban protegidos por placas óseas (el anillo esclerótico), que probablemente se ocupaban de mantener la forma de los globos oculares contra la presión del agua en las profundidades.

facts.statement: The size of the eyes and scleral rings suggests Ophthalmosaurus hunted in deep, dark waters or at night when prey was active.
facts.quote: El tamaño de los ojos y los anillos escleróticos sugieren que el Ophthalmosaurus cazaba en las profundidades donde no hay mucha luz solar o bien haber cazado de noche cuando sus presas eran más activas.

facts.statement: Calculations suggest a typical Ophthalmosaurus could remain submerged for approximately 20 minutes or more.
facts.quote: Los cálculos sugieren que un Ophthalmosaurus típico podía estar sumergido por aproximadamente 20 minutos o más.

facts.statement: Assuming a conservative swimming speed of 1 m/s, Ophthalmosaurus could dive to 600 meters and return to the surface in 20 minutes.
facts.quote: La velocidad de nado de Ophthalmosaurus ha sido estimada en unos 2.5 m/s o mayor, pero asumiendo una velocidad más conservadora de 1 m/s, un Ophthalmosaurus podría haber sido capaz de bucear a 600 metros y regresar a la superficie en 20 minutos.

facts.statement: Evidence in Ophthalmosaurus skeletons suggests it suffered from decompression sickness, possibly due to evasion tactics.
facts.quote: En las uniones óseas de los esqueletos de Ophthalmosaurus hay indicios que sufría del síndrome de descompresión, posiblemente a causa de sus tácticas de evasión.

facts.statement: The genus Ophthalmosaurus was named by Seeley in 1874.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Ophthalmosaurus (genus), Seeley 1874

facts.statement: Ophthalmosaurus belongs to the parent group Ophthalmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ophthalmosaurinae

facts.statement: Ophthalmosaurus is classified in the family Ophthalmosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Ophthalmosauridae

facts.statement: Ophthalmosaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Ophthalmosaurus lived from the Hettangian to the Valanginian, between 201.4 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Valanginian (201.4 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 27 recorded fossil occurrences of Ophthalmosaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 27
